a.text: The myriad souls lie prostrate.
Howling knocks on the door from beneath, tangible usurps the intangible.
Qui'sartuštaj bears witness.
The Black Crown imprisoned, the offender perpetually innocent.
Because kings are born before immortality.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Is W back yet?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The time she's spent on this mission has already exceeded our worst-case calculations.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How's Nightingale doing?

a.text: Shining looks past the window and at Nightingale, sleeping soundly under the trees outside.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Not great.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz has never been more stable than she is right now, but the amount of Originium in her body is rising, and it's highly likely her nociceptors will be affected.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This can't be an ordinary Infection symptom.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Perhaps it's due to the Sarkaz witchcraft devices on the battlefield, or maybe the whispering of the revenant... I don't know.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: There's no way I can tell Liz that 'I feel her pain'. For I have no idea what's going on.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: But yesterday, she was happily telling me how she hasn't been feeling any pain in her dreams for a long time now...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You're hesitating.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You've been like this ever since you returned from the Confessarius's place alone.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Do you remember what you told me, when you applied to come with me to Londinium?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: To 'heal Liz', Dr. Kal'tsit. This goal I've never wavered on, ever.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We may not know the exact status of her illness, but we all know what it means to 'heal' her.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: The things we need to do will not change... on this I'm clear.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have faith in you both.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The way you look at Nightingale isn't just with compassion. You're not just her doctor—she's healing your fears too.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Her body has its issues, but she's a member of the 'Followers', as well as your companion, and not a delicate flower that needs your protection.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Confessarii secret is truly a sickening affair, but we might only be able to uncover the truth by facing the abomination lurking in the utmost depths head on.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I know you may be somewhat worried.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But as I said when we first agreed to work together, Rhodes Island will help you if you ever need a hand.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: ——Thank you, Dr. Kal'tsit.

a.text: A blue fowlbeast chirps as it lands on Shining's shoulder.
This is Liz's usual way of greeting her.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz's awake. I'll go fetch her.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I'm fine, Shining. You don't have to look after me so meticulously.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz, we were just discussing your condition, and there are some signs... that aren't too great.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: The vicinity of Londinium has turned into a warzone, and there are some things that are affecting your health.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit and I are currently discussing our next course of action. This place is also just a temporary foothold.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Shining... come here. Closer.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Look at you. Why wear that face when you've already made up your mind?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: We can't run forever.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: The way things are now, we might as well confront them with our dignity intact, right?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I know you'll stay with me, so I'd rather stay here, and be a little more proactive.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Be strong, Shining. Your brows have been knitted ever since you met with them. Are you nervous?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Oh, right. While I was napping under the tree earlier... I had a dream.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I think we were children, walking in a stream...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: The water didn't even reach our calves. It was cold, but very pleasant. We didn't speak, only walking along quietly.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: And then I woke up. I saw a strange fowlbeast pecking at its own plumage.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: It seemed to be pecking at its bruise-covered body until it was entirely covered in blood...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: It gazed at me with a pleading look in its eyes, crying as it huddled in its own nest, but it was not liquid pouring down its face, it was white wax...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Even its mess of feathers were all frozen, and it was still chirping before it died—

a.text: Qui'sartuštaj bears witness.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: It was a strange melody, that sounded like...

a.text: Qui'sartuštaj bears witness.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: *Ancient Sarkaz Language*.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz...?

a.text: Shining spots a black fowlbeast resting on the tree, weakly nesting on a crown made of dead branches.
It looks back at Shining, and a trembling cry resounds from its syrinx, a rhythm permeating—
*Ancient Sarkaz Language*.
A black feather floats from the crown of dead branches.
It covers everyone's vision despite its tiny size.

steps.text: You led me here.
And so I've come to take you home, Liz.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (High-pitched braying)
Return from whence you came.
The structure is so fragile. It seems Theresis's blade is sharper than I imagined.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Watch out, Shining!

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: It's fine, Liz. He can't harm me.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: You've regressed.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: It will be a challenge to return your body to its peak condition. That will eat into my experimentation time.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: To think you'd willingly leave that sordid lair of yours...

a.text: The black fowlbeast rests on the dead branches in the Confessarius's hand.
Its robust body is covered by an abundance of feathers, shining with luster.
It was reborn so easily and instantly from corruption.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: It seems like you're anxious about something as well.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: We have already arrived at the gate.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: We've made great strides in our experiments, even just knocking softly on the door.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: You must attend the final ritual—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr, meltdown!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Angry howling)

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Five minutes will be enough, Salus. Stop her with your life.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Do not let them hinder me.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: Of course.

a.text: A black curtain of satin drapes down.
It binds the howling monster in multiple layers, giving it less and less space to struggle.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Pained howling)

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Her Arts are black...?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Is that... Amiya's? What have you done to her?!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They didn't defeat her.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: I should have been able to present the King of Sarkaz to the leader unharmed. It's a pity.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: But no matter. Even just getting a glimpse can let the fake take another step forward.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: So, little creature. Don't disturb our leader at work—follow me elsewhere to wait till he's done!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Angry wailing)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr!

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, you're in no shape to exert yourself.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I said last time that our next meeting would be on the battlefield.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Oh? Then why are you concealing your sword even now?

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: You swore to sever your ties with our lineage when you left home, and this whole time I've been looking forward for you to return and fulfil your promise.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: I gave you time, but you disappoint me again and again.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: We were supposed to produce the next me. We would have created the most intangible bloodline in the last hundred years.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Ugh...!

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Hm.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Sharp, but so impure. What's happened to your soul?

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Did you think you still had hope to cling onto, after leaving us?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz!

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Come back!

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I won't...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Let you manipulate me!

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Oh...? You're a creation that has surpassed my expectations.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: You're supposed to be just a shell, and yet you can touch 'me'?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Now, Shining!

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I... I can't hold on much longer!

a.text: A strange feeling surges from within Shining.
Nightingale is resisting the Confessarius, and even suppressing him—the ancient devil's soul has never manifested in such a vulnerable state before.
Bloodline. The word itself sounds unreal, but at this moment there only seems to be an extensive crack of blood right in front of her eyes.
But Shining hesitates.
Why is this so simple?
How could it be this simple?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Nightingale, stop!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's a trap! He's waiting for your Arts to resonate!

a.text: Time slows down.
Mon3tr fights with Salus as Kal'tsit yells out. Everything flows past like streams of light.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Both you and I know where fate will lead us, but those without self-awareness will only trap themselves in their own pitiful cage.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: It's futile to despise your bloodline and resist your fate. No one can deny the natural gifts bestowed by our bloodline.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: I will do for you what you're hesitating to do, to crack an opening in the cage... Enter it with me, and I will bring you back onto the right track.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Think it through before you make your choice...

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: *Ancient Sarkaz name*.

a.text: A white sword pierces though a heart atop a stone platform covered with dead branches.
Shining remembers the first time she cried, she remembers just how amazing it was, the birth of an unexpected emotion.
A brand new soul is carved anew under the blade.

steps.text: I've seen... pain... your... tears...

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Accidents are bound to bring surprises. You could have stopped your explorations here and now, but you just can't bear to destroy the ignorant consciousness in that hollow shell.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: And so you sew memories into the empty husk instead.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: She's Liz. She shouldn't...

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: You did this of your own free will, filled up this consciousness with a name, with 'Liz'.

a.text: 'Liz' is afraid of the completely silent person sitting across from her at the long table.
They agreed to sit here every night at the same hour for dinner together.
But the white-horned Sarkaz opposite her with a sword in her hands no longer speaks or moves outside of recording her every action she can remember today.
'Liz' always asks herself, have I done something to upset her?
'Liz' misses the beautiful memories, of how their lives were before...

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: I keep having the same dream every day. I dream of us as children, walking in a stream hand in hand...

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: Then I flew upwards, and kept going higher and higher. You couldn't hold me back, and I saw you crying from the clouds.

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: Every time, when I wish to return to your side, I always wake up in pain.

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: I ache from your suffering, and I want to bear it for you.

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: I just need you to tell me why you feel like this...

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: Qui'saršinnag.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Qui'saršinnag. This name means 'inseparable hope'—our destiny.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Poor 'Liz'. She think it's all her fault, because of the momentary kindness you showed her.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I've already abandoned that sinful name. I'm called Shining now, and will always be.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Is that so? Are you sure you can resist your family's destiny that has carried on for a millennium?

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: I'm looking forward to it.

a.text: 'Liz' holds the blue fowlbeast rescued from the river in her hands.
The indigo feathers are trembling, and the cold river water makes her shiver.
She thought Qui'saršinnag would get angry at her, but the sorrowful Sarkaz merely weaves a brand new birdcage for 'Liz'.
'Put it inside, and it'll stay safe always.'

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: I'm sorry, Qui'saršinnag. I didn't mean to endanger myself by going into the river to save it...

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: But I just couldn't watch it die.

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: I became fond of it the moment your family gifted it to me.

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: It likes to fly freely, but once it gets too far away from me it seems to lose its life, and falls into the river...

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: You say I did something similar yesterday... but I have no recollection of that at all.

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: But I'll listen to you, and put it inside the cage. I'll keep it safe.

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: Please don't get angry. I promise you something so foolish as this won't ever happen again.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: The cage has finally accepted their own duty, and you have also realized your own destiny.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: The more fragments and lies you fill her up with, the more confusion and suffering she goes through.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: I've lifted those dusty fragments for her. There's no undoing her awakening, and eventually, she will suffer as her rootless consciousness crumbles.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I won't let that happen, Father.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I'll end our sins with my own hands, and Liz will be 'cured'.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: And what next? Isn't her regaining the truth the very thing you fear, my dear sister?

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: This is the source of your woeful hesitation.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: I tolerate you wandering around with this receptacle, continuously strengthening this fragile cage...

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Because I trust you to cherish it with your all, and you never disappoint me.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Eventually you'll come back to my side with the cage in tow.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: That's what you've done. Look, She even tried to cage me in, to create an opportunity for you to defeat me.

spans.text: That's what you've done. Look, She even tried to cage
in, to create an opportunity for you to defeat me.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Your rebellious love for her, and her fate resisting conscience have sadly only become another catalyst together.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: —Even want to use the hope she found herself?!

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: Shining? Are you here?

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: I can sense your breathing, but I can't see you...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I'm here, Liz!

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: She can't hear your voice. We're walking within her tattered consciousness—

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: —Inside the cage.

a.text: Shining sees the blue fowlbeast, huge enough to fill her vision.
Giant gray eyes look down on her, she is unable to see herself reflected in those eyes.
The fowlbeast's sharp beak opens and closes, a mellow voice trails in from nowhere.

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: Shining... there's a vague question echoing in my head together with a name that stings me, but I can't recall it at all...

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: I might be able to remember it after we leave this place.

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: I've found I can share the pains of others and slow down their lives withering away.

steps.name: Liz?
steps.text: You said we'd go to faraway places to find a way to cure me, and maybe I can cure others in pain along the way too.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: She's submerged in those disorderly and fragmented memories, and will eventually lose herself in them.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Or perhaps she'll go mad, or maybe she'll end her own life before that happens.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: But you know how to solve this, Qui'saršinnag. I've taught you.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Draw your sword, and cut down your blood relatives here and now.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Our souls will reconnect with your sword as a bridge, and you—

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Will give birth.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: To ancient power.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: This is your inescapable destiny.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Become one with me, and use the remains of your bloodkin to nourish her consciousness that will stay shattered otherwise.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Forgive me, Liz.

a.text: Shining clutches the sword in her arms, and the Confessarius's hand is already pressing on the scabbard.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: At last, Qui'saršinnag...

a.text: Day and night are about to pour out from the sheath.
But a single hand holds onto Shining's sleeve.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Shining. I like your new name much better.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I feel like I've slept for a long time, lost myself within an infinity of fragments.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: But I heard your voice, and you guided me to a place buried underneath the countless fragments.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I dug up some of my splintered memories there... and I still haven't remembered them all.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: But I've recalled the question that I should have given you my answer to long ago...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I forgave you long ago.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Even before you resolved to seal all the memories of that laboratory away...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: So I'm angry with you for deciding to act on your own without asking me.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: 'Liz'. I've always loved the name you chose for me.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Don't run away and bear everything by yourself. Didn't we promise to face it all together—

a.text: Shining sees Nightingale's eyes, and her smile.
When she comes back to her senses, the hand has already quietly slipped away from her sleeve.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: A tragedy we have here, but the ending has already been determined.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: You killing me will turn you into the breeding ground for the next in our bloodline, or, you can look on helplessly as you watch me take her away and drown in your regrets after.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: It's all the same, Sister.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: Sir, we need to retreat!

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: Ugh!

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: How many bloodlines have you yet to touch, Chimera? Show me.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: How many times can you put blood back into your body, and tell yourself your own fate?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Confused growl)

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: (Angry howling)

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Excited cry)

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Your little monster's copy is quite poor.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Is this because you're not as strong as you were before your rebirth, or is Dame Kal'tsit, beloved of all tribes, even more injured than I thought?

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: (Disdainful roar)

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Qui'sartuštaj. The other part has chosen you.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: So what will you bring him?

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: The name 'Qui'sartuštaj' itself is the answer.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: (In ancient Sarkaz) 'Inextinguishable hope'.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Qui'saršinnag. The cage is already awake. If you continue to keep her by your side, she will only... like the dewdrops of early dawn, evaporate and fade away in the light.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: I will take her away, and I will help you maintain her, I will help you make amends—

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: I will forge this cage into a crown.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: And then, you will, we will be—

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: The King of Sarkaz for all eternity.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There's no point in chasing after him.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Take stock of our losses and prepare to move at once. We still have unstabilized wounded, but our cover here has already been blown.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Operator Nightingale is an employee of the Rhodes Island Medical Department, and we will not allow anyone to take her away or to do her harm.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But we might place her in greater danger if we make any rash moves. After all, we're facing an immortal 'Lord of Fiends' that has been coveting the crown for thousands of years.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Qui'sartuštaj. The one who knocks on the door, the King of Usurping Kings.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I knew the threat of the Confessarii since the days of Babel, even though my numerous countermeasure attempts were all in vain.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Theresis concealed them so well that everyone merely thought of them as the regent's guards.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Please be at ease. I know what we have to do now.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I thought you'd be less calm than this.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: What's your plan?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz... She has made her own choice.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: A choice even I had never dared to think of, daring, aggressive, and also the most effective method. It seems like the one afraid of loss and death has always been me...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: What I need to do. Heh.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Is to catch up to her.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...I believe in you both.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How's Amiya, Ascalon?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: She and the Doctor were also beset by the Confessarii's surprise attack, and are now with Logos.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Amiya has been affected by some kind of witchcraft. The one who they call Salus tried to seize the King of Sarkaz's power from her directly and failed, but Amiya's current condition is... very strange.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: She's fallen into a coma.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Amiya's connection with the 'Lord of Fiends' is only growing stronger, so we can only place our faith in her.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: We also discovered several of the Vampires' Arts Circles, accompanied by some 'illusions' from history.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: The Doctor mentioned that the Originium used to build these Arts Circles was very 'special'.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: 'Special'.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Well then, Lord Damazti, I thank you for your assistance. What do you seek from us?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We seek change. To hone ourselves. And meaning.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We seek the meaning of living a long and disordered life. You will show it to us, and we will verify it.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: ...That's all.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Tell Closure and Feist to sweep this place thoroughly. We'll leave in three hours.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Leave a message for W to head towards Brentwood as per our original plans.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We... really have to hurry.

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: Hey! Uncle Nowell! The lens in my glasses fell out again!

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: *Sigh*

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I told you so many times your ears are too soft.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You grip on the frames so hard every time you feel your glasses sliding down that you break and change their shape. So of course the lens won't stay in place.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Let me have a look.

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: It's because you gave me such a heavy pair to wear!

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: But I found a better method, look!

a.text: Little Susanna pulls out two leaves from behind her, and wedges the stems on her ears with the tips resting on her nose bridge.
Ah, glasses of green, fashioned with leaves.

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: Ta-da! What'd you think?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Can you see with them?

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: I can! Really!

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: Just face the sun, like this—

a.text: The child goes over to Nowell and puts two leaves on his eyes.
Nowell's vision is filled with a verdant green.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Alright, kid, you—

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: Just look!

a.text: Leaf veins.
The sunlight at noon in the forest is not very strong, but it is enough to shine through the thin leaves and reveal their interlaced veins, clear for all to see.

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: How is it? You can see, right?

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: You won't see anything interesting with that frown always on your face, Uncle Nowell!

a.text: He stares blankly at the sun with the leaves covering his eyes.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: ...I can't see anything at all.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: But, I know of a story from Yan of the east, a tale of 'missing the forest for the leaves'—

steps.name: Infected Child
steps.text: Nuh-uh, not listening! You're as boring as ever, Uncle Nowell!

a.text: The child with the glasses made of leaves comes and goes like a breeze, and disappears into the distant camp in the blink of an eye.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: It seems like you don't get along with the children, Mr. Nowell.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: If it isn't Talulah. Done with work?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I told that story to my son once... however, he didn't like hearing my stories either. Maybe I'm just not suited for it.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You have an abundance of experience, even if we only know it from a smattering of phrases.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: An average downtrodden Victorian optometrist who fled here after his shop was taken away from him amidst the war.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: He sympathized with the Infected who were being discriminated against, and so chose to join their group and help out a little with his abilities.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You've always displayed a respectable character ever since I got to know you, Mr. Nowell.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: But it's because of that... I...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Please speak your mind, Talulah.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm just curious why a long-lived like you would deign to conceal your identity and do such insignificant things.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I noticed. Of course, this is still much better than the worst-case scenario I thought of.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: However... you can deny it, and we'll speak of it no more. I'll tell Nine though.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I won't.

a.text: Nowell smiles, plucks a leaf and fiddles with it.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: There are actually many Victorians who I'm well-acquainted with, that know my identity... I only wish to avoid scaring my travel companions.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: But I'd like to correct you on one point, Talulah. I'm not 'deigning' to act like this.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: My longevity aside, I doubt I'm any more talented than ordinary people.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: The long-lived gain their longevity through different means, as diverse as the Originium Arts they use.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: But we aren't always influential figures, Talulah.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: In fact... I'm much more interested in your story.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: A descendant of the red dragon, founder of Reunion, and the leader of the Infected movement that took off in Ursus. To think you'd still act so shrewdly towards a so-called 'long-lived'?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...Who exactly are you, Mr. Nowell?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Just some guy.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: A hundred and fifty years ago, I was telling my third son the fables I learned from my travels in Yan, and he left my side from impatience.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: And as I stood before his granddaughter's granddaughter, I was once again a stranger in a large family.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: So now I harbor anger and pain inside me, giving up entirely on both family and love as I try to locate the villain hiding in Victoria who manipulated my fate.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I spent the last century researching... researching the ''long-liveds', the 'gods', the 'masterminds', the 'immemorials', and myself.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I tried to benefit from the system of nobility, to hone my Originium Arts, to accumulate wealth and exchange it for secrets...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I tried every method you can fathom to get closer to the truth, but I haven't been successful at all.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I didn't manage to become nobility or wealthy. I only had a little shop... that's all I really had. Combat abilities wise, I might not even be able to defeat Mr. Guard.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Time has only taught me to recognize the reality that I hold no talents at all.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: That's the story of an ordinary person, Talulah. This tale I can freely share with you.

a.text: Nowell drops the leaves that were in his hand, and the breeze blows them far away.
He dusts himself off, and picks up his suitcase once more.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Please, rest assured I hold no ill intent towards you all. I only wish to find... the 'hands of fate' that cursed me.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: She hides behind the country, treating her monarch as her glove, and the city-state her chessboard.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: She merely looks upon everything labeled 'Victoria' with a cold gaze. If needed, 'Victoria' can even be destroyed and rebuilt, and topped off with a new flag after.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: How can I believe she isn't involved in our current turmoil of absurdity?

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: She's definitely hiding within the dukes. Watching the Sarkaz and Victorians engage in mutual slaughter. Bloodshed and sacrifice are merely heartless parameters and indicators to her.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Perhaps you might have been manipulated by a similar pair of 'hands' before—you have royal blood running through your veins after all. She has no reason to let you nor Alistair's daughter go.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Me? I do know another conspirator, but he doesn't deserve to be called a god, nor can he manipulate my fate.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: But that's exactly how they live on, Talulah.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: I want to know how to kill them.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Or perhaps, how to kill myself.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: It's getting late, I need to fix little Susanna's glasses.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Mr. Nowell, you...

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: Talulah. The reason why I willingly tell you all of this, and why I joined Reunion—do forgive my selfishness—it is due to the intuition I've honed by the extra century I've lived.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: You too, have resisted such a predetermined fate.

steps.name: Nowell
steps.text: All of you here have.
